blocks.html: Short answer: For a first solo trip choose Chiang Mai (easy to get around, friendly); for mountains and a traveler scene, Pai; for a big city with great transport, Bangkok; and for islands where you will meet people, Koh Phangan or Koh Tao (learn to dive).

items.name: Chiang Mai
items.blurb: One of the easiest and safest cities to travel solo — walkable temples and cafés, cooking classes, hostels and a digital-nomad community where it is easy to meet people.

items.name: Pai (Mae Hong Son)
items.blurb: A laid-back small town with lots of solo travelers, friendly hostels and bars, and easy group tours — great for meeting new people in a relaxed setting.

items.name: Bangkok
items.blurb: A big city with convenient BTS/MRT, safe in the main areas, with hostels, cafés and food around the clock — ideal for solo travelers who want to move easily.

items.name: Koh Phangan
items.blurb: A party-and-yoga island where it is easy to meet travelers — the Full Moon Party, yoga classes and beach hostels, good for solo travelers who want to socialize.

items.name: Koh Tao (via Chumphon)
items.blurb: A diving mecca where cheap dive courses make it easy to meet coursemates — a small, easy island reached by boat from Chumphon, great for solo travelers who want to try diving.

faq.q: Is solo travel in Thailand safe?
faq.a: It is generally safe and traveler-friendly, especially in Chiang Mai and the main tourist towns. Mind your valuables, avoid empty areas late at night, check vehicles and boats, and watch your drinks at parties; solo women travel here fine with normal common sense.

faq.q: Where is easiest to meet other travelers?
faq.a: Pai, Koh Phangan and Koh Tao are easiest, thanks to hostels, group tours, yoga classes and dive courses, while Chiang Mai has cooking classes and a nomad community — stay in hostels or join activities to meet people faster.

faq.q: Can I travel solo without a car?
faq.a: Easily — Bangkok has the BTS/MRT and Grab, Chiang Mai and Pai have songthaews and motorbike rentals, and the islands use boats and local songthaews; everywhere on this list works solo without your own car.
